# Process / CLI I/O

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. What CLI tools and containerized services actually need day-to-day (argument parsing, stdin, environment config, exit codes). Prioritized because the long-term project direction favors CLI/microservice use cases. `console.log`/`.error` already write to stdout/stderr respectively — see [CONSOLE.md](CONSOLE.md) — the gaps below are everything *else* a CLI program needs.

**Coverage**: 33/33 (100%) · **Strict Coverage**: 19/33 (~58%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Command-line arguments (`process.argv`) | ✅ | | • Node's shape: `argv[0]` and `argv[1]` are the executable's absolute path (a compiled program is its own script), the arguments follow; an out-of-range read is `undefined`, and `process.argv0` is the operating system's `argv[0]` ([ADR-01278](../adr/ADR-01278.md)) |
| Environment variables (`process.env.KEY` / `process.env["KEY"]`) | ✅ | | • Both dot and bracket notation; a missing variable is `undefined` (`typeof` included), so `process.env.X ?? "default"` and narrowing behave as in Node ([ADR-01278](../adr/ADR-01278.md))<br>• On Windows it is the live Win32 environment read and written through the wide API (libuv's `uv_os_getenv`/`setenv`), not the C runtime's startup snapshot: non-ASCII values round-trip as UTF-8, lookup is case-insensitive as the OS's is, and a child spawned later inherits every write ([ADR-01032](../adr/ADR-01032.md)) |
